video_title: Content Creators calling out NBA and professional players?!!? Pat Bev REACTS

quotes.speaker: Patrick Beverley
quotes.summary_phrase: Patrick Beverley on his early career path to the NBA
quotes.excerpt: I kind of knew I belonged once I left college and I went to these UCLA runs.
quotes.quote: I kind of knew I belonged once I left college and I went to these UCLA runs. They had some runs in LA and I was just picking guys up full court and they didn't like it. I knew okay cool, I'm picking up Jordan Farmar, I'm picking up Jannero Pargo. These aren't caliber NBA names, but they are NBA players. If I can do that and lean my hat on that, I know once I get in the door I'll be okay.

quotes.speaker: Patrick Beverley
quotes.summary_phrase: Patrick Beverley on playing with European basketball legends
quotes.excerpt: We were all the same age. You talking about captains of some of the best European powerhouses.

text_blocks.speaker: Patrick Beverley
text_blocks.text: Kostas Papanikolaou, Sloukas, we were all the same age. You talking about captains of some of the best European powerhouses to ever play basketball. We were all the same age. We practiced against each other after practice, so my Greece ties go very deep.

text_blocks.speaker: Thanasis Antetokounmpo
text_blocks.text: Okay, so why were on, you played with all these European legends, right?

quotes.speaker: Patrick Beverley
quotes.summary_phrase: Patrick Beverley on his professional start in Ukraine and Greece
quotes.excerpt: My first professional team was a second division team in Ukraine. So I went from Ukraine, got drafted to the NBA, I spent one more year in Greece.
quotes.quote: I didn't know what Olympiacos, I didn't understand the team I was playing for at the time until probably five months into the season. My first professional team was a second division team in Ukraine. So I went from Ukraine, got drafted to the NBA, I spent one more year in Greece, which was the team with Olympiacos. A lot of people don't understand, I don't think they even know this, I tried out for Olympiacos and made the team. I didn't come in a situation where they wanted me. My agent knew someone, I tried out for Olympiacos, I just went there playing hard and I made the team.

quotes.speaker: Patrick Beverley
quotes.summary_phrase: Patrick Beverley on D3 players claiming they can dominate in Europe
quotes.excerpt: There's some superstars in the NBA right now that couldn't play in Europe. Just could not.
quotes.quote: There's some superstars in the NBA right now that couldn't play in Europe. Just could not. It's a different adjustment. It's team everything, coach runs everything. It's an adult college team. That's exactly what it is. It's team before any individual. We want to get a shot with six seconds on the shot clock, we lean our hat only on defense. It's a totally different game. The practices are totally different. You're going to compete every single day in practice, no days off really.

quotes.speaker: Patrick Beverley
quotes.summary_phrase: Patrick Beverley on his Indiana incident and regret
quotes.excerpt: What was said in Indiana was, I've never been spoken to that way my entire life in the NBA.
quotes.quote: What was said in Indiana was, I've never been spoken to that way my entire life in the NBA. I'm going to just say that. Do I regret the way I handled things? Of course. Could I have had handled things better? Of course. Obviously that you cross and you don't cross when it comes to just talking to anybody, any human being. And that line for the people that were around, that line was crossed several times. Did I handle it the best way? Probably not, but would that person go around saying those things again? Probably not.

quotes.speaker: Patrick Beverley
quotes.summary_phrase: Patrick Beverley on his goal to win a championship in Milwaukee
quotes.excerpt: I come to Milwaukee to only do one thing is to reach a pinnacle I've never reached before, win a championship.
quotes.quote: I come to Milwaukee to only do one thing is to reach a pinnacle I've never reached before, win a championship. I get a chance to play with Damian Lillard and I get a chance to play with Giannis Antetokounmpo. I played with every top wing in the NBA except him. When I got there I get to see how he works, what he's doing. I tried everything in my life to stretch that series as long as it can go. I don't think people understand that we were the only team in NBA history to win a playoff game without two of our main stars.

quotes.speaker: Patrick Beverley
quotes.summary_phrase: Patrick Beverley on his underdog mentality and public perception
quotes.excerpt: I think people misunderstand my passion for the game. It's an underdog passion.
quotes.quote: I think people misunderstand my passion for the game. It's an underdog passion. It's scratch and claw for everything type of passion. It's the long wolf, it's the journey. I bet on myself and I beat all the odds. When they see that type of passion mixed with me having to guard your favorite player, the second player, me having to guard the Stephen Currys who everyone loves, me having to guard the Westbrooks, I'm still accused for hurting Russell Westbrook initially, my first playoff game ever. When you kind of bottle that all in once, it looks like I'm public enemy number one.

quotes.speaker: Patrick Beverley
quotes.summary_phrase: Patrick Beverley on why you cannot bet against an underdog
quotes.excerpt: I know people in the Barstool, the cool people, they do their thing, but at the same time I know, come on, you cannot bet against the underdog.
quotes.quote: I know people in the Barstool, the cool people, they do their thing, but at the same time I know, come on, you cannot bet against the underdog. I'm sorry, I just won't. I refuse to bet against the underdog. I started my own thing from the beginning and no times soon you guys are going to be crushing it.

quotes.speaker: Patrick Beverley
quotes.summary_phrase: Patrick Beverley on his experience playing with superstars
quotes.excerpt: I've played in huge games. I've been fortunate to play with superstars, not a star, I've been fortunate to play with superstars.
quotes.quote: I've played in huge games. I've been fortunate to play with superstars, not a star, I've been fortunate to play with superstars. Anyone who challenges me when it comes to basketball, offensively in Europe, a juggernaut, defensively in the best league in the world, a juggernaut. I've only missed the playoffs one time. Superstars come get me. Hall of Fame coaches come get me. I know the game of basketball in and out.

quotes.speaker: Patrick Beverley
quotes.summary_phrase: Patrick Beverley on the Timberwolves not wanting him
quotes.excerpt: That game was against the team that essentially didn't want him.
quotes.quote: They don't know, because if they knew the narrative would be totally different. They don't know.

quotes.speaker: Patrick Beverley
quotes.summary_phrase: Patrick Beverley on why some creators don't play professionally
quotes.excerpt: A lot of these guys are not in professional leagues is because they either want to be in the NBA or don't want to play professionally.
quotes.quote: A lot of these guys are not in professional leagues is because they either want to be in the NBA or don't want to play professionally. That which is an insane concept, because playing basketball you have such a big privilege, because basketball is a global game. It's not like the NFL. The only way you can be a football player is the NFL. It's nowhere else. But basketball and making a living, you can go anywhere. You can go to Europe, Australia, Asia, anywhere you want to go if you're good at it. So that's the thing. I want to say close to 30% of those creators who are very, very good, but they just, is it their NBA or I don't want to play or I want to play doing playing one-on-ones.

quotes.speaker: Patrick Beverley
quotes.summary_phrase: Patrick Beverley on NIL as a semi-pro path for Europeans
quotes.excerpt: It helps the older guys that's overseas, right, because it takes some of the younger guys that's in Europe right now and they can go right to college.
quotes.quote: It helps the older guys that's overseas, right, because it takes some of the younger guys that's in Europe right now and they can go right to college. They can earn a lot more money and they can mostly live their NBA dreams. It's a semi-pro. That's all what NIL is, it's literally a semi-pro for Europeans. The game is reversed. You usually get the player, players not ready, in my case I go to Europe at a young age. Now it's the European who's not ready, he goes to college and earns a living. So I just think it's semi-pro just rolls reverse.

quotes.speaker: Patrick Beverley
quotes.summary_phrase: Patrick Beverley on the unique skill sets of NBA stars
quotes.excerpt: One of those guys can just throw the ball in the rim.
quotes.quote: One of those guys can beat you here, here, here, mechanical, Kawhi Leonard. One of those guys can beat you with strength, brute force, I'm going to run through you, I'm going to dunk on you. And one of those guys, you can literally just throw the ball and he can just do this. He can literally take the ball and just throw it in the rim. And when I speak about Giannis, with Victor Wembanyama he's a mix of all three of those guys. That's also 7'5. He's arguably the tallest player in the NBA. So when you get a player with that much skill, and mind you, he doesn't have to use his skill all the time. When you get any player where you could just throw the ball to, they can get the ball and they can just throw the ball in the hoop, it's nothing you can do with that. You just have to hope they miss.

quotes.speaker: Patrick Beverley
quotes.summary_phrase: Patrick Beverley on his experience in every NBA role
quotes.excerpt: I've been in every single role in the NBA.
quotes.quote: I've been in every single role in the NBA. I've been in Europe, here you go Pat Bev in Europe, here you go Pat Bev, it's seven on the clock, we need you to make a play. Okay, I'm not playing tonight, wave towel. I've been here, let me get the ball to the superstar. I've been a coach, don't run this, run another player. I've been in every role in the NBA.
